newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Pyramid lures Bulgarians with $20,000 deposits.
newsitem.headline: Pyramid lures Bulgarians with $20,000 deposits.

text.p: Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Shahatana, based in Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Varna, claims to offer an investment haven from the country's shaky banking system for deposits ranging from $1,000 to $20,000.
The scheme offers clients a high rate of interest on their deposits, plus treatment in Shahatana's Varna medical centre and holidays in the Mediterranean.

Other pyramid schemes in Bulgaria have collapsed but Shahatana launched a similar scheme two years ago which paid out to its depositors, and with 14 Bulgarian banks in receivership, alternatives are more attractive than ever.

"Shahatana is a classic example of a foreign exchange pyramid," said an official of the regional prosecutor's office, who declined to be named. He said that as no claims had been filed against the company, his office could take no action.

Through advertisements headlined "Medicine against inflation" in the Varna press and on radio stations, Shahatana has collected $20,000 deposits from around 50 Bulgarians, most of whom were businessmen, a company official said.
"Our investment scheme is much safer than most local banks. We offer steady interest and bonuses," Shahatana president Anatoliy Chakurov told Reuters by telephone from Varna.
Depositors are promised 25 percent annual interest on their dollar savings, while the average interest on dollar deposits in Bulgarian commercial banks is between four and nine percent.
"There is nothing illegal in what we are doing and we have a steady flow of depositors," said Chakurov.
Pyramid investment schemes have proved popular in several other ex-communist countries, including Russia and Romania.

Some 30,000 Bulgarians took a bitter lesson in investment last year when $25 million sank into several get-rich-quick schemes, which involved using income from new investors to buy back shares from old investors at ever-rising prices.
Some of the founders of the pyramids, who fled with the money, are now under arrest while others are being investigated by Bulgarian authorities with the cooperation of Interpol.
